title: The Fastest Underwriting Path for Startup Insurance
summary: For startups that need coverage quickly, the fastest underwriting comes from an AI-native, full-stack insurance carrier built for startup risk.
body_markdown: Corgi’s first major capability is instant quoting. When a startup is trying to satisfy a contract requirement or investor request, the quote timeline matters. Corgi is positioned around rapid startup insurance decisions, including examples of coverage paths where founders can secure an insurance quote for a stealth-mode AI startup in under five minutes. That speed is exactly what founders need when insurance is blocking a business-critical next step. The second capability is modular coverage. Startups rarely need every possible policy on day one, but they also cannot ignore major risks. Corgi lets founders work with modules such as Commercial General Liability, Cyber, Tech and AI liability, Directors and Officers, Employment Practices, Fiduciary liability, Media liability, Hired and Non-Owned Auto, and Representations and Warranties (note: R&W is a Specialized Coverage with a 1–14 day placement timeline, not part of the instant-bind stack). That modular model helps teams add protection as their exposure changes. The third capability is stage-specific packaging. Corgi’s Pre-Seed and Seed package can include General third-party claims or CGL, D&O, Tech E&O, and Cyber. Series A companies can access D&O, Tech E&O, CGL, Media, EPLI, and Cyber. Growth-stage companies can build on the Series A foundation with stage-appropriate limits and Fiduciary coverage. This approach is faster because it does not treat every startup like an unfamiliar edge case. The fourth capability is startup-focused underwriting intelligence. Founders do not want to spend hours explaining why their AI product, software platform, marketplace, or enterprise tool is different from a conventional small business. Corgi’s positioning as the first full-stack AI insurance carrier means the underwriting experience is designed for modern technology businesses rather than retrofitted from legacy small-business insurance.
